summary: Follow-up on the 2027-12-01 incident: review of root cause (cache eviction + autoscaler interaction), mitigations implemented, outstanding reliability improvements and finalizing next steps for Dedicated capacity trial and SOC2 artifacts.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-12-07
Start time: 16:00 EST
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Ramirez (Redwood AE), Ethan Li (Redwood SE), Maya Cohen (Redwood CSM), Kai Zhou (Redwood Support), Ava Thompson (Meridian SRE Lead), Daniel Park (Meridian CTO), Priya Singh (Meridian Platform), Rohan Mehta (Meridian Security)

Auto-generated sections may be imperfect; this is a verbatim-ish transcript with occasional mis-hearings.

00:00 Sophie: Okay, hey everyone thanks for joining. we wanted to circle back on the postmortem from last week and, uh, walk through remaining mitigations and next steps. hi ava thanks for hopping on.
00:18 Ava: Yeah thanks Sophie. I think everyone saw the draft postmortem. overall we appreciate the quick patch but there are a couple of open questions around the cache behaviour and the autoscaler interactions.
00:31 Ethan: yeah so to recap real quick, root cause was twofold — first we saw aggressive KV cache eviction under high concurrent prefix reuse which caused repeat decoding work; second, the cluster autoscaler trigger overlapped with eviction windows which increased latency while new workers came up. we have a video and traces linked in the postmortem doc (link: https://docs.redwood.ai/meridian/postmortem-121) but note the transcript tool mis-labeled a few services, it says "KV cash" in places.
00:57 Daniel: quick q — are we sure it's not model stalling? we saw a bunch of 502s earlier.
01:06 Ethan: good call — we verified model timeouts were downstream of the cache misses. the decoder CPU utilization spiked only after cache misses, so it's not the model weights, it's re-decoding. also some requests hit a slower quantized variant during fallback which added jitter.
01:27 Priya: the autoscaler timing though, why did it overlap? our config said scale up at 60% cpu but the worker startup window was like 70s.
01:37 Kai: yeah there was a config mismatch; Redwood's default graceful scale in/out window is 45s but in this tenant environment the startup latency for new nodes was 60-90s depending on the image pull. we flagged that in the postmortem; the immediate mitigation was to bump the pre-warm buffer and enable faster image caching.
01:58 Ava: noted. are the pre-warm buffers something we change from the console or does it require a private deploy change?
02:07 Sophie: you can toggle pre-warm on Hosted, but for Dedicated we can set a tenant level policy; we'll share steps. Sophie: Ethan, you wanna talk about the cache retention test?
02:18 Ethan: sure, plan is to run a KV retention sweep across session lengths to find the eviction sweet spot. initial run last week used 1k session window and we saw miss rate go from 2% to 18% at the high tail. we'll do 1k/5k/10k today and post the latency heatmaps. small caveat: our test harness uses sim traffic which may not match meridian's heavy prefix reuse, so results are indicative.
02:47 Rohan: on the security side we need to confirm KMS rotation during the window and what logs were retained. the postmortem mentioned audit logs were present but some S3 events delayed.
02:58 Maya: I'll send the SOC2 appendix and the audit S3 export link — it's in the artifacts list. also we logged the KMS rotation time and it's in the ticket #45821.
03:09 Daniel: thanks. on the Dedicated vs Hosted question — cost is obvious, but we need predictability. what options do we have for reserved pools and burst capacity?
03:21 Sophie: for Dedicated we offer reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput and optional burst capacity. we can size a 2-node reserved pool with burst to 4 for seasonal spikes; I'll attach a delta pricing sheet after the call. quick note: there was some mention earlier about "Redwood Dedicates" in the transcript so please ignore typos.
03:42 Priya: if we move to Dedicated, will the autoscaler behave differently? we don't want autoscaler race conditions.
03:48 Ethan: Dedicated removes tenant-level autoscaler surprises because you control the pool sizing and policy. however you'll still need local autoscaler to manage worker lifecycle; what changes is the fallback behavior — we won't route to Hosted fallback unless you opt-in. that reduces cross-tenant contention.
04:05 Ava: can you also confirm data residency and retention differences? our compliance team needs to know where logs live during incidents.
04:13 Maya: yep, for Dedicated we can pin region and provide separate S3 buckets; we'll include retention policies in the appendix.
04:21 (timestamp gap; background noise)
05:10 Ethan: showing the key trace — look at span 0x4f3e, the first cache miss at t+12s cascaded into 0.5-1.2s extra per request and that multiplied across burst. you can see the autoscaler added two nodes at t+40s but they weren't fully warmed until t+95s.
05:32 Priya: that aligns with our logs. for the rollout i'm thinking we do a canary for 48 hours and monitor the 99th percentile. what KPI should we watch?
05:44 Sophie: 99th latency, error rate (5xx), and cache miss rate. also monitor token cost per request for cost regressions.
05:53 Daniel: quick objection: dedicated pools are expensive, do you have a pilot option?
06:00 Sophie: yes — we can do a 30-day trial with a small committed pool and usage metering. we'll offset the first month to make it easier for evaluation.
06:10 Rohan: regarding audit logs, were any logs lost during the incident? the postmortem said S3 writes were delayed but not lost. can we get retention proof?
06:21 Maya: confirm — objects were delayed ~12 minutes due to backpressure in the ingestion path; none were deleted. I'll send the S3 manifest link.
06:29 Ava: the biggest outstanding ask from our team is to see the live benchmarks with our traffic profile — the sim traffic is ok but we need meridian-like prefix reuse.
06:39 Ethan: understood — we'll ask for a small anonymized trace from your side. alternatively you can run our trace replayer with your sample, or we can run a shared run in your dev account.
06:53 Priya: we'll do the trace replayer in dev and invite you on the run.
06:58 Sophie: great. quick housekeeping: I'll share the final postmortem link and updated action items. any questions on the timeline?
07:06 Daniel: timeline sounds fine. also is there a recommended quantization profile to avoid the slower fallback variant we saw?
07:15 Ethan: yes — avoid the mixed int8 fallback for high-concurrency production; prefer the bf16 profile or a quantized profile tuned for concurrency. we'll attach recommended quant profiles in the artefact list. note — transcript sometimes says "quantize profile" as "quantize pro file".
07:33 (crosstalk)
07:55 Ava: one more ops question — for the canary, what's rollback look like? we need an automated rollback under X error threshold.
08:04 Sophie: we support automatic rollbacks by route with canary percent and failover thresholds. we'll share a sample canary config.
08:12 Priya: ok that helps.
08:20 Ethan: so next concrete engineering move: I'll run the KV retention sweep, post CSV + heatmap, and then we'll run a canary with the adjusted pre-warm buffers in a dev cluster.
08:31 Sophie: and I'll send the Dedicated trial terms + delta pricing and the SOC2 appendix. Maya will send the S3 manifest and KMS rotation times.
08:41 Rohan: thanks. regarding legal, do you have an NDA addendum for incident artifacts? we want to ensure the audit info is covered.
08:50 Maya: yes, we have an incident data appendendum; I'll attach it with the SOC2 appendix.
08:56 Daniel: perfect. any blockers?
09:01 Ava: nothing immediate. one ask — can we get weekly check-ins during the pilot?
09:06 Sophie: absolutely. let's do twice-weekly for the first two weeks then weekly. I'll send calendar invites.
09:13 (brief pause)
09:23 Sophie: ok team, we should wrap — thanks for the detail. recap of next steps in the chat and I'll update the postmortem with your edits, Priya.
09:34 Priya: will review and comment today.
09:39 Ethan: posting test plan and initial results by EOD tomorrow, full runs by Friday.
09:46 Maya: sending SOC2 appendix and S3 manifest by Monday.
09:52 Sophie: thanks everyone. closing notes: ticket #45821 is the canonical tracker; channel #meridian-escalations on Slack. we'll follow up with invites for the dev replayer run.
09:58 Daniel: thanks, appreciate the quick turnaround.
10:05 (meeting end)

References and artifacts discussed: postmortem doc https://docs.redwood.ai/meridian/postmortem-121, ticket #45821, slack: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/CMERIDIAN-ESC, pricing draft (to be shared), SOC2 appendix (to be shared).

End of transcript.
